---
title: "Gene regulatory networks"
---

This chapter compares two sparse Gaussian graphical model (GGM) estimators
for cell-type gene networks: frequentist inference in `SILGGM`
[@zhangSILGGMExtensivePackage2018] and the Bayesian latent mixture in
`BLGGM` [@wuEstimatingHeterogeneousGene2022]. Both target a precision
matrix $\boldsymbol{\Omega}=\boldsymbol{\Sigma}^{-1}$, whose zeros encode
conditional independence [@friedmanSparseInverseCovariance2008]. Scripts:
`scripts/03_01_grn_silggm.R` and `scripts/03_02_grn_blggm.R`.

# Nonparanormal transforms in `huge` {#sec-glasso}

Count and compositional transcriptomes are not Gaussian. The SILGGM
workflow therefore Gaussianises the margins with `huge::huge.npn()`
before GGM inference
[@liuNonparanormalSemiparametricEstimation2009; @R-huge]. That
is the **nonparanormal / Gaussian copula** device: a latent Gaussian
vector is observed after unknown monotone transforms of each coordinate.

`huge.npn()` offers three `npn.func` values
([documentation for huge 1.3.5 / 2.0.1](https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/huge/versions/2.0.1/topics/huge.npn)):

| `npn.func` | What is computed | Role for GGM |
|------------|------------------|--------------|
| `shrinkage` (default) | Shrunken empirical CDF, then inverse-normal scores; returns an $n\times d$ matrix | Mild regularisation of the ECDF; usual default before `SILGGM` |
| `truncation` | Truncated ECDF (threshold `npn.thresh`, default of order $n^{-1/4}$) then inverse-normal scores; $n\times d$ | Winsorises extreme ranks; useful with heavy tails |
| `skeptic` | Nonparanormal skeptic: a $d\times d$ **correlation** matrix, not a data matrix | Copula correlation estimator; **not** a drop-in input to `SILGGM::SILGGM()`, which expects $n\times p$ observations |

For bulk or single-cell **compositions**, `shrinkage` or `truncation`
followed by a GGM is the practical Gaussian-copula path: the copula is
Gaussian after the marginal maps, while the observed scale stays
non-Gaussian. Use `skeptic` only when a correlation matrix is the object
of interest.

```{r}
#| label: npn-placeholder
#| eval: false
x_npn <- huge::huge.npn(x, npn.func = "shrinkage")
fit <- SILGGM::SILGGM(x_npn, method = "D-S_GL", global = TRUE)
```

# SILGGM versus BLGGM {#sec-silggm-blggm}

**SILGGM** is a frequentist toolkit for high-dimensional GGMs
[@zhangSILGGMExtensivePackage2018]. After optional NPN, it estimates
$\omega_{ij}$ (or de-sparsified versions) with nodewise scaled lasso,
de-sparsified graphical lasso (`D-S_GL`), or GGM estimation with FDR
control (`GFC_SL` / `GFC_L`). Global mode returns FDR-controlled
adjacency matrices. It does **not** model dropouts or unknown cell-type
mixtures: one typically subsets cells by annotation first.

**BLGGM** is a Bayesian latent Gaussian graph mixture
[@wuEstimatingHeterogeneousGene2022]. Observed (library-normalised)
expression $X_{gi}$ is a non-ignorable dropout of a latent Gaussian
$\theta_i$ with cell-type-specific mean $\boldsymbol{\mu}_k$ and precision
$\boldsymbol{\Omega}_k$, plus a spike-and-slab graph prior. MCMC (Gibbs +
HMC) yields posterior inclusion probabilities and FDR-style graph
cuts. It is built for zero-inflated, heterogeneous scRNA-seq, at a
higher computational cost (hours versus seconds) and a recommended gene
cap of a few hundred.

| | `SILGGM` | `BLGGM` |
|--|----------|---------|
| Likelihood | Gaussian (after NPN) | Latent Gaussian + dropout + mixture |
| Sparsity | $\ell_1$ / de-sparsified tests + FDR | Spike-and-slab + PPI |
| Heterogeneity | External labels | Joint clustering |
| Typical scale | Thousands of genes | $\lesssim 400$ genes |

Precision matrices feed the later contamination sweep (@sec-sensitivity).

# Launching jobs {#sec-cli}

```bash
nohup Rscript --no-save --no-restore scripts/03_01_grn_silggm.R \
  npn=shrinkage method=D-S_GL global=TRUE alpha=0.05,0.10 \
  input=data/processed/example.tsv \
  > "logs/03_01_silggm_$(date +%F)_shrinkage.log" 2>&1 &

nohup Rscript --no-save --no-restore scripts/03_02_grn_blggm.R \
  n_celltype=4 num_iterations=2000 num_threads=2 npn=none \
  input=data/processed/example.tsv \
  > "logs/03_02_blggm_$(date +%F)_K4.log" 2>&1 &
```
